notAnInstance.text: `{{slot}}` is a '{{source}}', accepted here as the class '{{target}}', and it is not an instance of that class. tsc compares classes by shape, and it compares a method's parameters in both directions, so a method that takes only a narrower type passes as one that takes any of the wider type, and fails at runtime when it gets one. In Adamic a class type means an instance of that class. Pass an instance of '{{target}}', or type the slot as an interface whose members are written property-style (`readonly admit: (animal: Animal) => string`), which tsc checks strictly.

typeArgumentsDiffer.text: `{{slot}}` is a '{{source}}', accepted here as '{{target}}'. A class's type arguments must match exactly: the class can write through them, and tsc compares its methods' parameters in both directions, so a `Box<Dog>` seen as a `Box<Animal>` can be handed a cat. Use the same type argument, or read the value through an interface with `readonly` members.
